account:
Today has mostly involved routine market visits, accounts, and appointments, but there are several unresolved bits of news. The neighbour says people are curious about lights at the bakery: the baker reportedly knew of no special occasion, and the builder said he had not installed them. There is also vague gossip about a crossing change, but no confirmed description or source. The builder reported the bridge passable, lanterns at both approaches and the center, no confirmed defects, and no recommended repairs. These reports do not establish any actual change to the crossing.

Residents saw the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and a sack of bread near the inn and plaza. The neighbour also saw the baker give bread to the freight carrier after a discussion about a market delivery. That could simply be ordinary bakery and delivery business. I personally saw freight hand a written book to the secretary before I left town hall, but I have not read it and do not know what it contains or whether it relates to the bread, lights, or crossing gossip.

My best provisional explanation is ordinary trade and deliveries alongside unexplained lighting and unverified crossing rumours. There may be something being arranged without my knowledge, but I have no evidence of wrongdoing or a common purpose connecting these observations. I should return for my sixteen-thirty office appointment and ask the secretary about freight's book, then seek firsthand information about the lights and supposed crossing change. My last request to the neighbour was not heard, so I cannot assume they will investigate for me.
